subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Sam / Anita —

Thanks again for taking the time today for the technical deep-dive. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the proposed Redwood approach, and agreed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Top pain points:
- Intermittent latency spikes for short queries during peak retail hours (promotions), impacting UX.
- Bursty traffic pattern: sustained baseline ~300 req/s but short bursts up to ~1,200 req/s for 1–2 minute windows.
- Hard requirement to keep 95th percentile tail latency under 200ms for 256-token requests.
- Need to support an LLM-backed product search reranker and short-form completion model with model comparability between on-prem and cloud (regulatory constraints).

Goals we heard:
- 95th < 200ms for short queries (<=256 tokens) across peak traffic.
- Sustained throughput target 500 req/s initially, ability to handle 1,200 req/s bursts for 2–3 minutes without user-visible errors.
- Regional failover for US east/west preferred; EU data residency for certain customers.

Model + inference requirements:
- Primary model: Llama-2-70B (quantized int8/int4 when possible) for reranking and completions.
- KV-cache persistence across short sessions would materially reduce cost/latency for multi-turn sessions.
- Deterministic tokenization and tooling to compare outputs between quantized and fp16 variants for evals.

Suggested deployment topology (Redwood):
- Start on Redwood Dedicated in us-east with a hot standby in us-west for region-level failover.
- Configure autoscale policy to keep a minimum pool to meet baseline 500 req/s and scale fast on bursts; enable burst capacity to handle 1,200 req/s for short windows.
- Use prefix/KV caching + request-aware batching for short queries to reduce p99/P95.
- Canary rollout: small % traffic to the quantized model variant, with automatic fallback to fp16 variant if latency or QPS thresholds are breached.

Attachments shared:
- redwood_slo_playbook.pdf (plays for latency & throughput tuning)
- acme_sample_load_test_plan.xlsx (sample JMeter/Locust plan + key metrics)

Agreed next steps:
1) Redwood: share load-test plan and initial canary config (attached). (Action: Marissa) — target: EOD Friday 2027-02-26
2) Acme: provide 1 representative production prompt set and token length distribution for top 10 queries. (Action: Sam) — target: Tue 2027-03-02
3) Schedule follow-up call with infra/ops to review networking and peering requirements (Target week of 3/8). (Action: Dylan to coordinate)

If this looks right, I will create the HubSpot tasks and upload the artifacts to the shared Drive link below.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- On the 95th < 200ms requirement: that target applies to the user-facing search reranker only (256-token avg). For batch re-ranks that run asynchronously we can tolerate higher tail latency.
- For model variants: are you recommending we start with fp16 on Dedicated and then canary to int8/4 quantized for cost savings? Concern is output drift; we need a clear regression plan.
- Multi-region failover is important but we need to understand the replication/window for KV caches — will the cache warm-up be problematic after failover?

I will gather the prompt set and token distribution and share before Tue. Also copying Anita (infra) to tee up the peering questions.

—Sam

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Great questions — answers inline below.

- Recommendation on variants: yes — start with fp16 to validate functional parity, then canary a quantized int8 (or int4 if quality checks pass) variant for cost/latency gains. We will provide a side-by-side eval harness (deterministic prompts + scoring) and automated regression alerts tied to your eval thresholds.

- Cache failover: KV cache is per-serving pool. For region failover we recommend a short overlap window with cross-region read-through on the hot standby for critical traffic (adds some network cost). If strict cold-start avoidance is required, we can pre-warm cache for top tokens via a scheduled warm job prior to failover events.

- Canary plan: we'll provide a canary config that routes 5% traffic to quantized variant for 24 hours with automatic rollback triggers on latency or output-regression thresholds.

I've uploaded the SLO playbook and the sample load test plan to the Drive link in the HubSpot deal; attaching stubs here as well.

Next call: Dylan, can you propose 3 slots for the week of 3/8 for infra/peering + load-test kickoff?

Thanks — M.
